Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

include verb

also including, be included, count in, count among, incorporate

classical

Quint. 1 pr. 21: liber prīmus ea quae sunt ante officium rhētoris continēbit
Traupman 140, 332

contineō, continēre, continuī, contentum

verb, second conjugation

include, contain, comprise

Of a whole that has the part in it: a book, a meal, a price. In the passive with the ablative, the part “is included in” it (Lewis & Short). “Including” is usually etiam or cum: omnēs, etiam līberī.

Other words

  • complector, complectī, complexus sum — embrace, take in, include

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.57: omnēs omnium cāritātēs patria ūna complexa est

    Of something that takes in many things at once.

  • inclūdō, inclūdere, inclūsī, inclūsum — put in, include (in a book, a letter)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.19.3: nēminem inclūdere in dialogōs; Cic. Att. 1.16.10: ōrātiōnem in epistulam (Lewis & Short)

    Its first sense is “shut in”: one includes something in a text, not a friend in a game.

  • in numerō habēre — count among, include in a group

    phrase: numerus in the ablative, with a genitive · also used · classical · Cic. N. D. 3.48: in deōrum numerō habērī (Lewis & Short); Cic. Phil. 2.33: mē adscrībe tālem in numerum (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s mē adscrībe tālem in numerum is “count me in that number”.

Examples

  • Cārī sunt parentēs, cārī līberī, propinquī, familiārēs, sed omnēs omnium cāritātēs patria ūna complexa est

    Dear are our parents, dear our children, our relatives and friends; but our country alone includes all our love for all of themCic. Off. 1.57

  • nam liber prīmus ea quae sunt ante officium rhētoris continēbit

    for the first book will include what comes before the teacher of rhetoric takes overQuint. 1 pr. 21

  • sīc enim cōnstitueram, nēminem inclūdere in dialogōs eōrum quī vīverent

    for I had decided to include in my dialogues no one who was still aliveCic. Att. 13.19.3

See also involve, group, member.
